_THE_FRAMING_TO_PRESERVE.this_is_NOT_an_STR_identity_problem: The STR profile -- 16 markers, 15 STR loci plus amelogenin, over the 18 lines of the Cellosaurus `ST` block -- is concordant across three independent sources (Cosmic-CLP=907290; DepMap=ACH-001519; RCB=RCB0508) and Cellosaurus carries NO 'CC Problematic cell line:' flag for CVCL_1238. The line is authentically itself.
_THE_FRAMING_TO_PRESERVE.it_IS_a_disease_label_problem: What is in doubt is whether the line is the DISEASE it is named for. EMC is defined by NR4A3 rearrangement under current criteria.
_THE_FRAMING_TO_PRESERVE.why_the_two_must_not_be_conflated: The large cell-line-integrity literature (ICLAC, the Register of Misidentified Cell Lines, HeLa cross-contamination, STR authentication mandates) is almost entirely about a line being A DIFFERENT LINE. A line that is correctly itself but mislabelled AS TO DISEASE is a distinct failure mode. Any future search that lets these collapse together will return a false 'already covered'. THIS IS THE MOST LIKELY WAY TO GET THE WRONG ANSWER.
_THE_FRAMING_TO_PRESERVE.the_fairness_constraint: Fusion-negative EMC TUMOURS are a recognised entity in the clinical literature (see established_findings.fusion_negative_emc_is_a_real_category). So 'H-EMC-SS is fusion-negative' does not by itself mean 'wrongly diagnosed'. Any write-up must engage this honestly rather than treating the label as simply an error, and must never impute error or bad faith to named authors.

the_one_published_observation.title: SLFN11 is Widely Expressed in Pediatric Sarcoma and Induces Variable Sensitization to Replicative Stress Caused By DNA-Damaging Agents.
the_one_published_observation.authorString: Gartrell J, Mellado-Largarde M, Clay MR, Bahrami A, Sahr NA, Sykes A, Blankenship K, Hoffmann L, Xie J, Cho HP, Twarog N, Connelly M, Yan KK, Yu J, Yu J, Porter SN, Pruett-Miller SM, Neale G, Tinkle CL, Federico SM, Stewart EA, Shelat AA.
the_one_published_observation.verbatim_quote: Although extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) cancers such as H-EMC-SS typically have EWSR1-NR4A3 fusions, we did not detect a EWSR1 -translocation in this line.
the_one_published_observation.location: Figure 2A legend. Verified verbatim in the fetched full text (S9).
the_one_published_observation.what_it_is_not: Not an EMC paper and not an identity paper. Its subject is SLFN11 in paediatric sarcoma across a ~20-line panel in which H-EMC-SS is one member. Repo commit 842961ad2 established: no results sentence, figure, table or supplement reports the assay for this line; the 'n >= 2' in that legend is the drug-assay replicate count; the methods' PCR/FISH sentence is a blanket statement over the whole panel naming no probe, no primer and no per-line result; and the paper does not state whether an EWSR1 break-apart FISH (which WOULD exclude EWSR1::NR4A3 whatever the partner) or an EWSR1-FLI1 RT-PCR (which would NOT) was performed.
the_one_published_observation.significance: THIS IS THE NEAR-MISS AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR ANY NOVELTY CLAIM. The observation is in print. 'Nobody has ever reported this' would be FALSE. What is true is that it has never been the subject of anything, nothing downstream follows from it, and it is not discoverable by anyone searching on EMC model validity.

the_database_annotation.the_asymmetry_ESTABLISHED: The record ships the DISEASE ASSIGNMENT to every downstream consumer via 29 DR cross-references (DepMap ACH-001519; Cell_Model_Passport SIDM00535; Cosmic/Cosmic-CLP/GDSC 907290; ECACC 94042258; RCB RCB0508; PharmacoDB HEMCSS_419_2019; ChEMBL; LINCS_LDP LCL-1458; FANTOM5_SSTAR; Progenetix; PubChem_Cell_line; Wikidata Q54871889; ICLC HTL99016; and others). The CAUTION travels with none of them. This asymmetry — a silent flag in one registry against a disease label propagated everywhere — is, on the evidence gathered, the most defensible core of any write-up.
the_database_annotation.note: So the answer to 'how is this handled in practice' is, for this one line: a database caution field, citing a figure legend, with no correspondence, no erratum and no change to the disease assignment.

exposure_triage._status: PARTIAL — TITLE/ABSTRACT LEVEL ONLY. Only one of the 43 papers (Gartrell, PMID 34413129) was read in full text. Five further full texts were fetched in S10 and never read (PMC9813045, PMC5509331, PMC13273627, PMC6516718; PMC10054153 returned 404).
exposure_triage._universe: 43 Europe PMC records name the line under any of H-EMC-SS / HEMC-SS / HEMCSS / H-EMC SS (S1). Union with "EMC-SS" adds 2.
exposure_triage._criterion_used: TIER A — the paper's stated conclusion is about EMC as a disease entity or about NR4A3/the fusion, and H-EMC-SS is the or a principal experimental basis; relabelling changes what the conclusion is ABOUT. TIER B — the paper attaches a disease label to the line but its claim is about chondrosarcoma generally, or the line is one of a panel; relabelling changes a descriptor, not a result. TIER C — no disease-specific claim; the line is used as a generic human/chondrocytic/mesenchymal cell. DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE: one line among fourteen in a drug panel is NOT an EMC claim.

FINDING_1_the_most_important_one.statement: ZERO of the 43 papers makes a claim about NR4A3, the fusion, or fusion-driven biology derived from this line. Exactly ONE of 43 abstracts contains any fusion term at all (MED:36316541), and there the fusion terms describe EMC tumours in general and the authors' two NEW ex vivo models — not H-EMC-SS.
FINDING_1_the_most_important_one.consequence: THE EXPOSURE IS NOT 'CONCLUSIONS ABOUT FUSION BIOLOGY ARE WRONG'. Nobody drew any. The exposure is narrower and different in kind: therapeutic and phenotypic claims are ATTRIBUTED TO A DISEASE the model may not represent. Any write-up that implies the fusion literature is contaminated by this line would be overstating it, and the triage does not support that.

FINDING_2_label_distribution_from_abstra.line_not_characterised_in_abstract: the remainder — many use it as a generic human cell (e.g. GH/UCP signalling, heparan-sulfate epigenetics, Hsp90 solvent mapping, fibrillin/LTBP profiling)

FINDING_3_highest_exposure_candidates_TI.why: Abstract verbatim: 'using the human extraskeletal myeloid chondrosarcoma cell line (HEMC-SS)' — 'myeloid' appears to be a typographical slip for 'myxoid'; the label attached is nonetheless extraskeletal.

FINDING_4_a_concentrated_single_group_ex.observation: A substantial share of the corpus is one research programme (proteoglycan/quaternary-ammonium targeting and hypoxia-activated prodrugs) using this line as its principal in vitro and xenograft model across many years: MED:21499733 (2012), MED:24972007 (2014), MED:29221170 (2017), MED:30199705 (2018), MED:32948981 (2021), MED:36582458 (2022), MED:37689817 (2023).
FINDING_4_a_concentrated_single_group_ex.why_it_matters: If a correction is ever warranted, its practical weight falls disproportionately on one group's model choice rather than being diffuse across the field. ⚠ STATE THIS NEUTRALLY. These authors mostly describe the line as 'chondrosarcoma', consistent with the supplier's own catalogue entry, and the fusion-status information did not exist in an accessible form until 2021 at the earliest.
FINDING_4_a_concentrated_single_group_ex.counted_how: membership read off titles/abstracts in S1; NOT verified against author lists or affiliations

FINDING_5_a_second_independent_label_que.observation: Most of the corpus uses the line as a model of CHONDROSARCOMA (a cartilage tumour). EMC is not classified as a cartilaginous tumour under current criteria — MED:36316541's abstract states verbatim: 'Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) is a malignant mesenchymal neoplasm of uncertain differentiation as classified by the WHO Classification of Tumours 2020.'
FINDING_5_a_second_independent_label_que.why_it_matters: This is a SEPARATE labelling issue from the fusion question and predates it. A paper that framed everything as 'the fusion is missing' would miss that the larger exposure by paper count is the chondrosarcoma-vs-EMC gap, which does not depend on the fusion finding at all.

novelty_verdict._status: CANNOT BE ISSUED — the category search (the half that decides it) was never read.
novelty_verdict.what_IS_established: On this LINE: the fusion-negative observation exists in print (Gartrell 2021 figure legend) and as a Cellosaurus caution. It has never been the subject of a paper, letter or commentary in the searches actually read (S1–S6). A claim of 'never reported' would be false; a claim of 'never examined, and never propagated to the databases that carry the disease label' is supported by what was read.
novelty_verdict.what_is_NOT_established: Whether the CATEGORY (authentic-but-disease-mislabelled models) already has a literature, a name, or a handling convention. This is the question that decides whether there is a paper here at all, and it is exactly the question left open.

paper_or_letter._status: PROVISIONAL — do not act on this without the category search.
paper_or_letter.reasoning_from_what_was_established: The narrow finding is small: one line lacks one lesion, already noted once in print and already flagged in one database. On its own that is CORRESPONDENCE, not a paper — and arguably not even that, since Gartrell 2021 and Cellosaurus between them have already said it. The thing that could carry a paper is the ASYMMETRY (see papers_on_this_line.the_database_annotation.the_asymmetry): a caution that stops at one registry while the disease label propagates through ~29 cross-referenced resources into DepMap, GDSC/COSMIC, PharmacoDB, LINCS and FANTOM5. Whether that is novel depends entirely on the unread category search — specifically the Cellosaurus 'hallmark'/cc:caution censuses, which would establish whether this is one instance or a class with an N.
paper_or_letter.what_would_make_it_a_LETTER: if the category turns out to be well described and only this line's instance is new
paper_or_letter.what_would_make_it_a_PAPER: if the Cellosaurus census shows a class of such lines, and no existing literature names or monitors the failure mode
paper_or_letter.what_would_make_it_NEITHER: if a model-fidelity or authentication paper already covers disease-label mismatch as a recognised category — the outcome the framing note warns is easiest to miss

what_it_would_argue._status: SKETCH ONLY, not validated against the category literature.
what_it_would_argue.the_one_sentence: STR authentication certifies that a cell line is itself, and nothing in the current authentication regime asks whether it is still the disease it is named for — so a line can be flawlessly authenticated, sold as the reference model for a rare cancer, and lack that cancer's defining lesion, with the disease label propagating through every downstream resource while the doubt stays in a single caution field.
what_it_must_NOT_claim: that the ~37 papers' results are wrong — the triage found zero fusion-derived claims among them
that this is a misidentification or contamination — it is not, and conflating them is the central error to avoid
that any author erred — the supplier catalogue, the databases and the publication timeline all supported the label they used
any count, date or identifier not re-verified from a source
what_it_would_argue.the_honest_missing_piece: No wet-lab confirmation is possible here. The fusion-negative call rests on DepMap's filtered fusion caller (2 calls, neither naming NR4A3 nor any FET gene), floor-level NR4A3 expression, the absence of a Cellosaurus gene-fusion line, and one figure-legend sentence whose assay is not specified. That is suggestive and consistent, not definitive, and must be stated as such.
